chapter: Later tours, illness and the union job
title: Playing the Brussels Fair with Sidney Bechet
summary: Clayton recalls Bechet's fury over 'Royal Garden Blues' in Marseilles and then playing the 1958 Brussels Fair with him, Bechet's last engagement.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: But I had been there many times. I went and played at the World, Brussels Fair for Sidney Becket. Now this was in '58, 1958. This was Vic Dickenson, myself, Arvell Shaw, Kansas Fields, George Wein on the piano.
Now I think I remember you saying that that was a very great experience.
What was it that you, particularly impressed you or what was it you found so much.....
I don't know. I remember one time I was on a bill with Sidney Becket, not playing with him, when I had my band with me, Merle Stepton and Bishop and we met in Marseilles.

Now I'm supposed to play the first half and he's supposed to play the second half. So we played and we played a number, 'Royal Garden Blues'. Boy he got furious because we played that. That's his number. We weren't supposed to play Dixie land numbers. Oh he raised hell. He blew his top. He used to blow up, you know like quit and walk off the stand and go home. He did everything but cuss
me out, for playing 'Royal Garden Blues'. And I didn't know that he was like that. I say anybody can play it.
Well there were hundreds of numbers so... (LAUGHTER).

Sure there's a lot of other numbers. But no, that was, I wasn't supposed to do that. So when he wanted me to come to play in Brussels with him I kind of thought it was, it would be nice to play with him because I'd never played with him and he had a big name. He was one of the greatest jazz men over there, you know.

So I felt this was a very nice thing. And by that time he was kind of mellow. He gotten a lot older and he used to talk to me and he says "yes," you know, "don't work too hard now. Don't let nobody take advantage of you" and things like that. Then he'd go to sleep.
You see that was his last engagement and he never made any more engagements.
Really? That one he played with you?
That was his last record date, too.
